subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the economic development indicator GNI stand for?
questions.explain: GNI (Gross National Income) is the total value of goods, services and income earned by a country's people and businesses, often given per capita.

questions.q: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite measure that combines which three elements?
questions.explain: HDI combines life expectancy (health), years of schooling (education) and GNI per capita (income) into a single value.

questions.q: On what scale is the Human Development Index (HDI) measured?
questions.explain: HDI is expressed as a value between 0 and 1, with figures closer to 1 showing higher levels of development.

questions.q: Why can GNI per capita be a misleading indicator of a country's development?
options: It is an average that hides inequalities within the country
It only measures the birth rate
It cannot be calculated for large countries
It ignores a country's total wealth
questions.explain: As an average it conceals the gap between rich and poor, so a high figure may still mask widespread poverty.

questions.q: The infant mortality rate measures the number of deaths of children under one year old per how many live births?
questions.explain: Infant mortality is the number of babies who die before their first birthday per 1,000 live births in a year.

questions.q: In the Demographic Transition Model (DTM), which stage shows a rapidly falling death rate but a still-high birth rate, causing rapid population growth?
questions.explain: In Stage 2 improved food and healthcare cut the death rate while birth rates stay high, so the population grows quickly.

questions.q: Country X has a GNI per capita of $1,200, a life expectancy of 58 and a literacy rate of 55%. Using the IMF classification used by OCR, Country X is best described as a(n):
questions.explain: Low income, short life expectancy and low literacy are typical of a Low-Income Developing Country (LIDC).

questions.q: Which of the following is a physical (environmental) barrier to development?
questions.explain: A landlocked location is a physical barrier because it raises trade costs and reduces access to sea ports.

questions.q: Why does dependence on exporting primary products (raw materials) tend to slow a country's development?
options: Their prices are often low and fluctuate, giving unstable income
They can only be sold to neighbouring countries
They are always taxed by the United Nations
They cannot be transported by sea
questions.explain: World prices for raw materials are low and unpredictable, so earnings are unstable and add little value compared with manufactured goods.

questions.q: A country's development being held back by its past rule under a European empire is an example of which type of barrier?
questions.explain: Colonialism is a historical barrier, as former colonies were often exploited for resources and left with weak economies.

questions.q: Frank's dependency theory argues that development is held back because:
options: Wealthy 'core' countries exploit poorer 'periphery' countries, keeping them dependent
All countries pass through the same five stages of growth
Countries near the Equator can never industrialise
Population growth always outstrips food supply
questions.explain: Dependency theory sees rich core nations exploiting poor peripheral nations, trapping them in an unequal, dependent relationship.

questions.q: How does international debt act as a barrier to development?
options: Repaying loans and interest diverts money away from spending on development
It automatically lowers a country's birth rate
It prevents a country from trading any goods
It increases the number of doctors available
questions.explain: Money spent repaying loans and interest cannot be invested in schools, healthcare or infrastructure, slowing progress.

questions.q: Malaria, a barrier to development in some tropical LIDCs, is spread by which vector?
questions.explain: Malaria is spread by mosquitoes and reduces development by causing illness and death that weaken the workforce.

questions.q: A country spends around 40% of its export earnings repaying loans from overseas banks and governments. This best illustrates which barrier to development?
questions.explain: Using a large share of export income for loan repayments is a clear example of debt limiting development.

questions.q: How many stages are there in Rostow's modernisation (stages of economic growth) model?
questions.explain: Rostow's model has five stages, from traditional society through to the age of high mass consumption.

questions.q: Which statement best describes 'intermediate (appropriate) technology' as a development strategy?
options: Small-scale, affordable technology suited to local skills and resources
Large, expensive high-tech machinery imported from advanced countries
Technology that can only be used by trained engineers
Fully automated factories run by robots
questions.explain: Intermediate technology is small-scale and affordable, matching local skills so communities can maintain it sustainably.

questions.q: How does Fairtrade aim to help producers in developing countries?
options: It guarantees them a fair, more stable minimum price plus a premium for their goods
It removes all taxes on imported machinery
It provides emergency food during droughts
It cancels a country's international debt
questions.explain: Fairtrade guarantees a fairer minimum price and an extra premium, giving farmers more reliable incomes to invest in their communities.

questions.q: Why is microfinance considered an effective bottom-up development strategy?
options: Small loans let ordinary people, often women, start their own businesses
It is a single large loan given to the national government
It provides free imported manufactured goods
It builds large dams to generate electricity
questions.explain: Microfinance gives small loans to individuals, often women, enabling them to set up small enterprises and improve local livelihoods.

questions.q: An LIDC frequently suffers droughts that destroy its rain-fed crops. Which strategy would most directly improve food and water security for its rural farmers?
questions.explain: Affordable small-scale irrigation directly tackles water shortages for farmers, improving crop yields and food security.

questions.q: A women's cooperative in an LIDC receives small loans to buy sewing machines and set up a tailoring business. This is an example of which development strategy?
options: Foreign direct investment by a TNC
questions.explain: Providing small loans to individuals or cooperatives to start businesses is microfinance.
